His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Ha Mim﴾ ﴿By the Clear Book﴾. Its explanation has already been given (in Surah al-Mu'min and Surah al-Zukhruf). The answer to the oath is ﴿Indeed, We sent it down﴾. The pronoun "it" refers to the Book, which is the Qur'an, ﴿on a blessed night﴾. Regarding this night there are two opinions.

The first: it is the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr), which is the view of the majority. ʿIkrimah related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: The Qur'an was sent down from the presence of the Most Merciful on the Night of Power all at once, and it was placed in the lowest heaven, and then it was sent down in installments. Muqatil said: The entire Qur'an descended on the Night of Power from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven.

The second: it is the night of the middle of Sha'ban, as stated by ʿIkrimah.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We are ever warning﴾, meaning: warning (people) of Our punishment.

﴿Therein﴾, meaning: in that night, ﴿every matter is made distinct﴾, meaning: is separated and decided. Abu al-Mutawakkil, Abu Nuhayk and Muʿadh al-Qari read "yafraqu" with a fatha on the ya and a kasra on the ra, and "kulla" with a fatha on the lam, ﴿every wise matter﴾, meaning: firm and decreed. Ibn ʿAbbas said: From the Mother of the Book, on the Night of Power, is written what will occur in the year of good and evil, sustenance and lifespans, even the pilgrim (to Hajj). You may see a man walking in the markets while his name has already been entered among the dead. According to what is narrated from ʿIkrimah that this occurs on the middle night of Sha'ban, the narration from him in this regard is unstable, and the narrator has been contradicted in it. It is narrated from ʿIkrimah that he said: It is on the Night of Power, and this is the view of the commentators.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿As a command from Us﴾. Al-Akhfash said: "amran" and "rahmatan" are in the accusative as circumstantial clauses (ḥāl); the meaning is: "Indeed We sent it down, commanding a command and showing mercy with mercy." Al-Zajjaj said: It is also permissible that it be in the accusative governed by "yufraqu," in the sense of "yufraqu farqan," since "amran" means "farqan." Al-Farra' said: It is also permissible that "rahmah" be in the accusative by the action of "mursilin" upon it, so that the mercy is the Prophet ﷺ. Muqatil said: "Mursilin" means "munzilin" (those who send down) this Qur'an; We sent it down as mercy for whoever believes in it. Others said: ﴿As a command from Us﴾, meaning: We command the abrogation of what is abrogated from the Tablet. ﴿Indeed We were ever sending﴾ the Messengers, ﴿as a mercy﴾ from Us to Our creation. ﴿Lord of the heavens﴾: Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu ʿAmr and Ibn ʿAmir read "Rabbu" with a damma. Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim read "Rabbi" with a kasra on the ba'. What follows up to His saying is clear, until ﴿Nay, they are in doubt﴾, meaning the disbelievers, ﴿about what We have brought them﴾, ﴿playing﴾, meaning mocking at it.

(p-339) ﴿So watch for the day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke﴾ — that is, wait for it. The scholars differ over this smoke and its time, giving three opinions.

The first: it is a smoke that will come before the Hour. It has been related from Ibn ʿAbbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "The smoke will come and seize the breaths of the disbelievers, while it will affect the believers like a cold (zukam)." Ibn Abi Malaykah narrated: I went to Ibn ʿAbbas one day and he said: "I did not sleep last night until morning." I asked: "Why?" He said: "The comet with the tail rose, and I feared the smoke would come upon us." This view is also reported from ʿAli, Ibn ʿUmar, Abu Hurayrah, and al-Hasan.

(p-340) The second: the Quraysh were struck by famine, and they saw between themselves and the sky a smoke from hunger. Al-Bukhari and Muslim in the two Sahihs related from the hadith of Masruq, who said: "We were with ʿAbdullah (Ibn Masʿud), when a man entered upon us and said: 'I came to you from the mosque, and I left a man saying about this verse, ﴿the day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke﴾: a smoke will cover them on the Day of Resurrection, seizing their breaths, so that it will affect them like a cold.'" ʿAbdullah said: "Whoever has knowledge should speak of it, and whoever does not know should say: Allah knows best. This was only because the Quraysh, when they defied the Prophet (ﷺ), he invoked against them with years like the years of Yusuf, so a drought and hardship struck them, until they ate bones and carrion, and a man would look at the sky and see between himself and it something like smoke from hardship." They said: ﴿Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed we are believers﴾. (p-341) Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We will remove the punishment a little; indeed, you will return﴾. So He removed it from them, but they returned to disbelief, and so they were seized on the day of Badr. That is His saying: ﴿the day We will strike with the greatest assault﴾." This is also the view of Mujahid, Abu al-ʿAliyah, al-Dahhak, Ibn al-Sa'ib, and Muqatil.

The third: it is the day of the conquest of Makkah, when the sky was veiled with dust. This is related by al-Mawardi.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿This is a painful punishment﴾ — that is, they say: this is a punishment.

﴿Our Lord, remove from us the punishment﴾ — regarding this there are two opinions: the first, hunger; the second, the smoke. ﴿Indeed we are believers﴾ in Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an.

﴿How will they have the reminder?﴾ — that is, from where will they have remembrance and admonition after the descent of this trial, while ﴿there had already come to them a manifest Messenger﴾ — that is, one clearly truthful?!

﴿Then they turned away from him﴾ — that is, they turned away and did not accept his word, and they said: ﴿a taught, possessed man﴾ — that is, he is one taught by a human who is possessed, through his claim of prophethood. The first: the harm that befell them was lifted by plenty; this is according to the view of Ibn Masʿud. Muqatil said: He lifted it until the day of Badr.

The second: it is the smoke, said by Qatadah.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed you will return﴾ — regarding this there are two opinions: the first, to polytheism, said by Ibn Masʿud; the second, to the punishment of Allah, said by Qatadah.

Allah's words: ﴿That deliver﴾, meaning: deliver to me, ﴿the servants of Allah﴾. On this there are two opinions.

According to this, "the servants of Allah" is in the accusative as a vocative (an-nida'). Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning would be: "Deliver to me what I command you, O servants of Allah."

The second: send with me the Children of Israel. This was said by Mujahid and Qatadah, and the meaning is: release them from your subjugation and hand them over to me.

﴿And that you not exalt yourselves against Allah﴾. On this there are three opinions. The first: do not fabricate lies against Him, said by Ibn Abbas. The second: do not transgress against Him, said by Qatadah. The third: do not be arrogant toward Him, said by Ibn Jurayj. ﴿Indeed, I am bringing you a clear authority﴾, meaning: a proof that indicates my truthfulness.

When he said this, they threatened him with killing, so he said: ﴿And indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from your stoning me﴾. On this there are two opinions.

The first: it is stoning with words, said by Ibn Abbas; the meaning is that they would say: "He is a poet or a madman."

The second: it is killing, said by al-Suddi.

(p-343) The second: he was noble before his Lord; this was said by al-Farra'. The third: he was of honourable lineage and of a middling, respectable descent; this was said by Abu Sulayman.

Allah's words: ﴿That deliver﴾, meaning: deliver to me, ﴿the servants of Allah﴾. On this there are two opinions.

The first: deliver to me what I call you to of the truth by following me. Al-Awfi narrated this meaning from Ibn Abbas. According to this, "the servants of Allah" is in the accusative as a vocative (an-nida'). Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning would be: "Deliver to me what I command you, O servants of Allah."

The second: send with me the Children of Israel. This was said by Mujahid and Qatadah, and the meaning is: release them from your subjugation and hand them over to me.

﴿And that you not exalt yourselves against Allah﴾. On this there are three opinions. The first: do not fabricate lies against Him, said by Ibn Abbas. The second: do not transgress against Him, said by Qatadah. The third: do not be arrogant toward Him, said by Ibn Jurayj. ﴿Indeed, I am bringing you a clear authority﴾, meaning: a proof that indicates my truthfulness.

When he said this, they threatened him with killing, so he said: ﴿And indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from your stoning me﴾. On this there are two opinions.

The first: it is stoning with words, said by Ibn Abbas; the meaning is that they would say: "He is a poet or a madman."

The second: it is killing, said by al-Suddi.

﴿And if you do not believe me, then leave me alone﴾, meaning: leave me, neither with you nor against me. So they disbelieved and did not believe. ﴿So he called to his Lord: "These are a criminal people."﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: whoever opens the "anna" (that), the meaning is "because these are"; whoever breaks it (inna), the meaning is: he said, "Indeed these are," since "inna" after a verb of saying takes the kasra. The exegetes said: "the criminals" here refers to the polytheists.

(p-344) So Allah answered his supplication and said: ﴿So set out with My servants by night﴾, meaning the believers, ﴿indeed, you will be pursued﴾, pursued by Pharaoh and his people. Thus He informed them that they would be pursued, and that this would be the cause of their drowning.

﴿And leave the sea at rest﴾, meaning: leave it still in its state after it has parted for you, and do not command it to return as it was until Pharaoh and his hosts enter it. Ar-Rahw means walking in tranquility.

Qatadah said: when Musa, peace be upon him, crossed the sea, he turned back to strike the sea with his staff so that it would close up, fearing that Pharaoh and his hosts would follow him. So it was said to him: "And leave the sea at rest," meaning: as it is, a dry path.

Allah's words: ﴿Indeed, they are an army to be drowned﴾. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed him of their drowning so that his heart would be at peace in leaving the sea as it was.

﴿How many they left behind﴾, meaning: after their drowning, ﴿of gardens﴾. We have explained this verse in [ash-Shu'ara: 57]. As for "ni'mah" (blessing), it is a comfortable, abundant life. What follows this has already been explained [Ya-Sin: 55], up to His words: ﴿And We made them an inheritance to another people﴾, meaning the Children of Israel.

﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾, meaning: over the family of Pharaoh. On its meaning there are three opinions.

The first: it is literal. Anas ibn Malik narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no Muslim except that he has two doors in the sky: a door through which his deeds ascend, and a door through which his provision descends. When he dies, they both weep over him." And he (ﷺ) recited this verse. Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "When the believer dies, his place of prayer on earth weeps over him, and the place from which his deeds ascend in the sky weeps. The family of Pharaoh had no place of prayer on earth nor a place of ascent for deeds in the sky, so Allah the Exalted said: 'So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them.'" To this view went Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, and Muqatil. Ibn Abbas said: the redness that is in the sky is its weeping. Mujahid said: No believer dies except that the heaven and the earth weep over him for forty mornings. It was said to him: "Do they weep?" He said: "Why would the earth not weep over a servant who used to cultivate it with bowing and prostration? And why would the sky not weep over a servant whose glorification and magnification in it sounded like the hum of bees?"

The second: the intended meaning is the people of the heaven and the people of the earth. This was said by al-Hasan. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿Until the war lays down its burdens﴾ [Muhammad: 4], meaning: the people of war.

The third: the Arabs say, when they wish to magnify a great destruction: "The sun was darkened for him, the moon eclipsed at his loss, and the wind, the lightning, the sky, and the earth wept for him," intending exaggeration in describing the calamity. This is not a lie on their part, because they all (p-346) agree on it, and the listener knows the speaker's intent. Their intention in saying "the sun was darkened" is: it nearly became dark; and "the moon eclipsed" means: it nearly eclipsed. The meaning of "kada" (nearly) is: he intended to do something and did not do it. Ibn Mufarragh said, lamenting a man:

"The wind weeps for his grief, and the lightning flashes in the clouds."

Another said:

"The sun is rising, not eclipsing, weeping for you, along with the stars of the night and the moon."

He meant: the sun is rising, weeping for him, and it does not, by its rising, eclipse the stars and the moon, since it is dark; it only eclipses by its light, and the stars of the night are visible by day. So the meaning of the statement is: when Allah destroyed the people of Pharaoh, no weeper wept for them, no grieving one grieved, and no loss was felt. All of this is the words of Ibn Qutaybah.

The commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on Surah 44, verses 30–42:

His saying, ﴿from the humiliating torment﴾, means the killing of the sons, the enslavement of the women, and the toil in Pharaoh's labors. ﴿Indeed, he was haughty﴾, i.e., a tyrant.

﴿And We chose them﴾, meaning the Children of Israel, ﴿over knowledge﴾, knowledge that Allah had of them, ﴿over the worlds of their time﴾. ﴿And We gave them of the signs﴾, such as the parting of the sea, the shading of the clouds, the sending down of the manna and quails, and other things, ﴿wherein was a clear trial﴾, i.e., a manifest blessing.

Then he returned to mention the disbelievers of Makkah, saying: ﴿Indeed, these ones say﴾, ﴿"There is only our first death, and we will not be resurrected. So bring back our fathers, if you are truthful."﴾ "Our first death" means the death that occurs in this world. ﴿And we will not be resurrected﴾, i.e., we will not be raised up. ﴿So bring our fathers﴾, i.e., raise them up for us, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ about the resurrection. This was ignorance on their part for two reasons.

The first: they had already seen signs sufficient for proof, so they had no right to be excessive in their demands.

The second: the restoration is for recompense, and that is in the Hereafter, not in this world.

Then he warned them of the torment of the nations before them, saying: ﴿Are they better﴾, i.e., stronger and mightier, ﴿or the people of Tubba'?﴾ i.e., they are not better than them. Wahb said: "Tubba' embraced Islam, but his people did not embrace Islam, so his people are mentioned and he is not mentioned." Some of the exegetes mentioned that he used to worship fire, then he embraced Islam and invited his people, who were Himyar, to Islam, and they denied him.

As for his being named "Tubba'" (a title for the kings of Yemen), Abu ʿUbaydah said: every king of the kings of Yemen was called Tubba', because he follows (yatba'u) his companion. So the position of "Tubba'" in the Jahiliyyah is like the position of the caliph in Islam. Muqatil said: he was named Tubba' because of the multitude of his followers, and his name was Malkaykarib. He mentioned the people of Tubba' because they were closer to the destruction awaiting the disbelievers of Makkah than others were. What follows this has already been discussed [Al-Anbiya: 16; Al-Hijr: 85], up to His saying: ﴿Indeed, the Day of Decision﴾, which is the day on which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will decide between the servants. ﴿Their appointed time﴾ means their appointment, ﴿all of them﴾, to which the first and the last will come.

One: no close relative will benefit a close relative. This is the view of Muqatil. Ibn Qutaybah said: no protector will avail a protected one by kinship or otherwise.

(p-349) The second: no cousin will benefit his cousin. This is the view of Abu ʿUbaydah.

﴿Nor will they be helped﴾, i.e., they will not be prevented from the torment of Allah, ﴿except for those on whom Allah has mercy﴾, and they are the believers, for some of them will intercede for others.

Whoever recited "taghli" with the ta', it is because the tree is feminine; whoever recited with the ya', he took it as referring to the food. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: It is not permissible to take the boiling (al-ghali) as referring to al-muhl, because al-muhl was mentioned as a comparison in melting, and only that which is compared to it boils: ﴿like the boiling of boiling water﴾, which is hot water when its boiling becomes intense.

(p-350) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Seize him﴾, meaning: it will be said to the guards (al-zabaniyah): seize him ﴿and drag him﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Ibn Amir, and Yaqub recited with a damma on the ta'; the rest recited with a kasra. Ibn Qutaybah said: its meaning is: drive him with violence; it is said: "So-and-so was brought, being dragged (ya'tali) to the ruler." And "sawa' al-jahim" means the middle of the fire. Muqatil said: the verses concern Abu Jahl; an angel of the keepers of Hell strikes him on his head with an iron mace, so that it breaks open his brain, and his brain flows over his body. Then the angel pours into the opening scalding water whose heat has become extreme, and it enters his belly. Then the angel [says to him]: ﴿Taste﴾ the punishment, ﴿indeed you are the mighty, the noble﴾. This is a rebuke to him by that; Abu Jahl used to say: "I am the most mighty and most noble of Quraysh." Al-Kisa'i recited "dhuq annaka" with a fath on the hamza; the rest with a kasra. Abu Ali said: whoever recited with a kasra, the meaning is: you are the mighty in your own claim; whoever recited with a fath, the meaning is: "because you."

If it is said: how was he called "the mighty" when he was not?

The answer is in three ways.

The first: it was said as mockery toward him; this was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Muqatil.

The second: you are the mighty [and noble] in your own estimation; this was said by Qatadah.

The third: you are the mighty among your people, the noble among your family; related by al-Mawardi.

Then He mentioned the abode of the God-fearing, saying: ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing are in a secure station﴾. Nafi and Ibn Amir recited "fi muqam" with a damma on the mim; the rest with a fath. Al-Farra' said: al-maqam with a fath on the mim means the place, and with a damma means the staying.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿secure﴾, meaning: they are safe therein from harm (al-ghayr) and misfortunes. We have already mentioned "the gardens" in [Al-Baqarah: 25], and we mentioned the meaning of "the springs" and "facing each other" in [Al-Hijr: 45, 47], and we mentioned "fine silk and brocade" in [Al-Kahf: 31].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thus﴾, meaning: the matter is as We have described, ﴿and We will pair them with huur 'iin (wide-eyed maidens)﴾. The commentators said: the meaning is: We will join them with them, and it is not from the contract of marriage (tazwij). Abu Ubaydah said: the meaning is: We made the males of the people of Paradise mates (azwaj) ﴿with huur 'iin﴾ from the women; you say to a man: pair this single shoe with the single shoe, i.e., make them a pair; the meaning is: We made them two and two. Yunus said: the Arabs do not say "tazawwaja biha"; they say "tazawwajaha." The meaning of ﴿We paired them with huur 'iin﴾ is: We joined them. Ibn Qutaybah said: it is said: "zawwajtuhu imra'atan" and "zawwajtuhu bi-imra'atin." Abu Ali al-Farisi said: the revelation is according to what Yunus said, which is His saying: ﴿We married her to you﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 37], and not "We married you to her."

As for al-huur, Mujahid said: al-huur are women of purest whiteness. Al-Farra' said: al-hawra' is the white (female) camel; he said: in "huur 'iin" there are two dialects: "huurun 'iinun" and "hiirun 'iinun," and he recited:

Ah, a long-eyed woman, joy of the traveler, and a white-eyed woman with the wide eyes of the hiir.

Abu Ubaydah said: al-hawra' is the one of extreme whiteness of the white of the eye, extreme blackness of the black of it. We have already explained the meaning of "'iin" in [As-Saffat: 48].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿calling therein for every fruit, secure﴾. There are two opinions regarding this. One: secure from their being cut off in some seasons. The second: secure from indigestion, illnesses, and calamities.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿except the first death﴾. There are three opinions regarding this.

One: it means "besides" (siwa), so the sense of the statement is: they do not taste death in Paradise, besides the death they tasted in the world; similar is: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already passed﴾ [An-Nisa': 22], and His saying: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾ [Hud: 107], i.e., besides what your Lord wills for them of addition beyond the measure of the world. This is the view of al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj.

The second: when the blessed die, they arrive at rest, sweet fragrance, and means of Paradise, and they see their dwellings in it; and when they die in the world, it is as if they died in Paradise, because of their connection to its means and their witnessing of it. This was said by Ibn Qutaybah.

The third: that "illa" means "after," as we mentioned in one of the views on His saying: ﴿except what has already passed﴾ [An-Nisa': 22]. This is the view of Ibn Jarir.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿as a bounty from your Lord﴾, meaning: Allah did that for them as a bounty from Him.

﴿So indeed We have made it easy﴾, meaning: We made it easy, the reference being to the Qur'an, ﴿in your tongue﴾, meaning: in the language of the Arabs, ﴿so that they may remember﴾, meaning: so that they may take heed and believe. ﴿So wait﴾ (p-353), meaning: await punishment for them; ﴿indeed they are waiting﴾ for your destruction. This verse, according to most commentators, is abrogated by the verse of the sword; but this is not correct.
